body_text:
Two sets $A$ and $B$ have the same cardinality if there exists
a bijection $A\to B$. We write $|A|\leq|B|$ when there exists
an injection $A\to B$. A set is finite if it is bijective with
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ for some natural number $n$; it is countably
infinite if it is bijective with $\mathbb{N}$, and countable if
it is finite or countably infinite.
